cards.explanation: The answer is the simple and the young. Verse 4 says the book gives prudence to the simple, and knowledge and discretion to the young. Two groups, two gifts. I think it's good news for anybody still learning, friends, because nobody has to walk in already knowing it all. I started out in a bin with a 25 cent sticker, so I'm very pro-beginner.

The answer is False. Verse 5 says, “…let the wise listen and gain instruction, and the discerning acquire wise counsel” The wise aren't excused from the book, they're invited into it. They're the ones told to listen. Being wise just means you keep listening.

The answer is the fear of the LORD. Verse 7 says, “The fear of the LORD is the beginning of knowledge…” That's the starting line, friends, before any single proverb gets going. Knowledge begins right there.

The answer is True, and it's all in one verse. Right after naming where knowledge begins, verse 7 goes on, “…but fools despise wisdom and discipline.” The word but sets the two sides side by side. The beginning of knowledge on one side, and what fools despise on the other. Short verse, big contrast.

The answer is his mother's. Verse 8 says, “Listen, my son, to your father’s instruction, and do not forsake the teaching of your mother.” So the father's instruction and the mother's teaching are both named in the same verse. The son is told to listen to the one and not forsake the other.

The answer is a garland and a pendant. Verse 9 says, “For they are a garland of grace on your head and a pendant around your neck.” One goes on the head and one goes around the neck. The voice reaches for things a person wears, friends. Nothing in this verse is armor.

The answer is True. Verse 10 says it plainly: “My son, if sinners entice you, do not yield to them.” Entice means they'll try to pull him in. The instruction is to not yield. It's a short sentence, and the voice doesn't dress it up.

The answer is innocent. Verse 11 has the sinners saying, “…let us ambush the innocent without cause…” The people they're after have done nothing to deserve it. I think this one hurts to read. The sinners say it right out loud in their pitch.

The answer is plunder. In verse 13 the sinners say, “We will find all manner of precious goods; we will fill our houses with plunder.” Notice it's a pitch, friends. Right alongside the goods, they talk about lying in wait for blood in verse 11. Plunder is the prize they're offering.

The answer is False. Verse 15 says, “…do not walk the road with them or set foot upon their path.” The instruction covers walking with them at all, not only the ambush itself. The voice says it twice in one verse, once as the road and once as the path.

The answer is that their feet run to evil. Verse 16 gives the reason: “For their feet run to evil, and they are swift to shed blood.” It's about where they're headed and how fast they move. That's why the son is told not to set foot on their path. The path leads where their feet are running.

The answer is their own. That's the twist, friends. Verse 18 says, “But they lie in wait for their own blood; they ambush their own lives.” Back in verse 17 comes the line about spreading the net where any bird can see it. Then verse 18 says the sinners are lying in wait for their own blood. The ambush they talked about is aimed at their own lives.

The answer is all who are greedy. Verse 19 says, “Such is the fate of all who are greedy, whose unjust gain takes the lives of its possessors.” Remember the plunder and the shared purse from their pitch? The verse says the fate belongs to all who are greedy. Their unjust gain takes the lives of those who hold it.
